questions.question: Which adapter method determines if the current environment can support the adapter?
options: initialize() — it tries to start and catches errors
canActivate() — it inspects the environment before starting
start() — it returns false if the platform is unsupported
getEndpoint() — it probes the network stack
questions.explanation: Correct! canActivate() is the guard method. Native checks for __ALLTERNIT_RUNTIME__, MCP checks for process, CLI always returns true.

questions.question: The MCP adapter's McpStorageBackend sets isPersistent = false. What does this mean for a plugin using host.storage.set()?
options: The storage call throws an error
Data is stored in-memory only and lost on restart
Data is written to a temporary file
The call is silently ignored
questions.explanation: Correct! The MCP storage uses an in-memory Map. When the MCP server process restarts, all stored data is gone. Plugins should check host.storage.isPersistent before relying on long-term state.

questions.question: When the HTTP adapter receives a request with options.stream = true, what protocol does it use to send real-time updates?
options: Long-polling with repeated HTTP GETs
Server-Sent Events (SSE) with text/event-stream
gRPC streaming over HTTP/2
Raw TCP socket
questions.explanation: Correct! The HTTP adapter sets Content-Type: text/event-stream and sends SSE events: start, then complete (or error).

questions.question: The Native adapter checks globalThis.__ALLTERNIT_RUNTIME__. Why does it use globalThis instead of window or global?
options: Because Allternit runs in a Service Worker
Because global is deprecated in Node.js 20+
Because it works in both browsers and Node.js without platform detection
Because window is blocked by Content Security Policy
questions.explanation: Correct! globalThis is the standard ECMAScript reference to the global object, working in browsers, Node.js, Deno, and Web Workers without conditional checks.

questions.question: In the MCP adapter, what happens when a plugin function returns an artifact of type image?
options: The adapter wraps it in an MCP { type: 'image', data, mimeType } content block
The adapter converts it to base64 text and sends type: 'text'
The adapter ignores it because MCP doesn't support images
The adapter writes it to disk and returns a file path
questions.explanation: Correct! The MCP adapter inspects result.artifacts and wraps image artifacts as { type: 'image', data, mimeType } blocks in the MCP content array.

questions.question: Which adapter provides session.getHistory() that returns actual conversation history rather than an empty array?
options: HTTP Adapter — it caches history in the server
MCP Adapter — Claude provides the history
Native Adapter — it forwards to runtime.session.getHistory()
CLI Adapter — it reads from a local JSON log file
questions.explanation: Correct! Only the Native adapter forwards getHistory() to the Allternit runtime. All other adapters return an empty array because they don't have access to the host platform's conversation history.
